title: martius-lab/lodos
abstract: # Lodos Lodos is a *research codebase* for running massively parallelized simulations of rigid-body dynamics with contact. It is particularly optimized for achieving high-throughput in scenes involving collisions between large numbers of detailed meshes. The main repo is https://github.com/martius-lab/lodos The framework builds upon two of our previous works: * `papers/lodos_v1.pdf`: The first version of the framework, under review. The current codebase incorporates significant extensions beyond this initial version, as described in `papers/lodos_v2.pdf`. These developments will eventually find their way into a follow-up publication. * `papers/contact_tutorial.pdf`: A tutorial on discrete time-stepping methods for simulating cone-complementarity-based contact dynamics. It concludes by proposing a general proximal minimization blueprint, and this codebase essentially constitutes a concrete implementation. From an implementation perspective, Lodos is built entirely using [NVIDIA Warp](https://nvidia.github.io/warp/). Its architecture builds upon a core subset of the [MJWarp](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_warp) codebase, particularly its constraint model and its excellent GPU implementation of a nonsmooth Newton solver with exact line-search. ## How to Get Started? * Read through `papers/lodos_v1.pdf` and `papers/lodos_v2.pdf` to understand the context around Lodos and its contributions. * Read through `papers/contact_tutorial.pdf` to understand the theory behind Lodos. * Read `viewer/README.md` to run interactive simulations of an existing catalogue of scenes. * Read `bench/README.md` to reproduce the benchmark comparing Lodos to [MJWarp](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_warp) and [Kamino](https://disneyresearch.github.io/kamino-site/). * Run the examples in `notebooks/` to familiarize yourself with the API. * Read `tools/performance_tuning/README.md` to understand how to tune Lodos simulations to maximize throughput. * Read `tools/mesh_processing
